parts.problem_md:
Fig. 2.1 shows a section of a plant stem.

![Microscope cross-section of plant stem showing labelled outer layer, central xylem tissue and region Q within vascular bundle](assets/001-microscope-cross-section-of-plant-stem-showing-l.png)

(i) Circle the substances transported by the cells labelled **Q** on Fig. 2.1.

**      amino acids                 fatty acids                   glycerol                   glucose                                                                              nitrate ions                   starch                       sucrose**

[1]

(ii) One function of xylem is transport.

State one other function of xylem.

[1]
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - (i) Sucrose and amino acids circled **[1 mark]**
> - (ii) Support **[1 mark]**
> 
> More than two circled = 0 marks

> **[exam-tip]**
> Phloem transports the products of photosynthesis and protein building (sucrose and amino acids), while xylem transports water and minerals — keep these two transport tissues and their cargo separate.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a cross-section through a leaf.

![Diagram of a leaf cross-section showing upper epidermis and several circular cells, with one labelled X and a larger central oval cell in the middle](assets/002-diagram-of-a-leaf-cross-section-showing-upper-ep.png)

What are the functions of the tissue labelled X?

1. transport of amino acids
2. transport of sucrose
3. transport of water
4. support
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- Tissue X is xylem
- Xylem transports water (3) and provides structural support (4) to the plant

**A** is incorrect because amino acids and sucrose are transported in phloem, not xylem

**C** is incorrect because amino acids are transported in phloem, not xylem

**D** is incorrect because sucrose is transported in phloem, not xylem
